page: Microsoft Azure FX48-12mds_v2 is a constrained-core virtual machine configured for high memory capacity per core and fast single-threaded clock rates. It operates on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor using the x86_64 architecture, providing 12 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 6 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at 4.2 GHz. The CPU features a 260 MB L3 cache alongside support for AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets. Memory provision is exceptionally dense at 1008.0 GB of RAM, equating to 84.0 GB per vCPU. The server bundles 2835 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and includes zero GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier single-core performance, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2365.0 and strong text processing at 2927.0. Single-threaded compression throughput is similarly competitive, reaching 34.55 GB/sec in gzip compression and 14.47 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics reflect the constrained 12 vCPU limit, registering average-tier outcomes across PassMark CPU (22868.23) and multi-core Geekbench (11420.0). Uncached memory bandwidth reaches 102.55 GB/sec for large block reads and 73.18 GB/sec for writes.

The primary tradeoff of the FX48-12mds_v2 lies in its restricted core count relative to its massive RAM footprint. While qualitative cost efficiency is reduced for general parallel computation due to paying for high-memory density and high base clocks, the design is highly cost-effective for per-core licensed software environments. By constraining the allocation to 12 vCPUs while retaining access to over a terabyte of memory and 2835 GB of high-speed local NVMe storage, licensing overheads can be minimized substantially.

The hardware profile fits large in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA), relational databases with per-core licensing (such as SQL Server or Oracle), and caching layers like Redis, which achieved 18.91 million SET operations per second in testing.

Built on the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz, it provides 12 dedicated vCPUs (6 physical cores) paired with a massive 1008.0 GB of RAM (84.0 GB per core) and a 260 MB L3 cache. It incorporates 2835 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and contains no discrete GPUs. Benchmarks show top-tier single-threaded compute, scoring 2365.0 in Geekbench single-core and 34.55 GB/sec in gzip compression, while multi-core metrics remain moderate due to the restricted thread count. Local memory bandwidth reaches 102.55 GB/sec for uncached read blocks. This configuration optimizes operational efficiency for large in-memory databases, electronic design automation, and commercial enterprise engines requiring extensive memory without core-based licensing penalties.
